lines: This plan covers 3 days, starting today.
A session is set for Wednesday: you cook on Thursday and Saturday, and nothing cooked then can feed the days before it. It is a day you did not ask for.
To stay inside it, expensive proteins give first, then out-of-season produce, then variety — never the portions.
You asked for crunchy: there isn't any this time.

dishes.name: Cocoa oat crunch
dishes.title: Soy yoghurt, gluten-free oats, cocoa and pumpkin seeds
dishes.method: Spoon the yoghurt into a bowl and scatter over the oats, pumpkin seeds and cocoa.
dishes.why: This is a substantial no-cook breakfast before the extra Wednesday kitchen session.

dishes.name: Chickpea crunch plate
dishes.title: Chickpeas, cucumber, green pepper and rice cakes
dishes.method: Slice the cucumber and pepper. Toss them with the chickpeas, lemon juice, rapeseed oil, salt and pepper, then eat with the rice cakes.
dishes.why: The chickpeas anchor a quick lunch while cucumber and green pepper provide the green crunch requested.

dishes.name: Smoky lentil skillet
dishes.title: Warm lentils, potatoes, courgette and green pepper
dishes.method: Cook the smoky lentil and potato skillet during the Wednesday session and serve one portion immediately while hot. Cool and refrigerate the second portion promptly for Thursday.
dishes.why: The hot lentil skillet gives dinner a warm anchor without turning Wednesday into a long batch-cooking evening.

dishes.name: Cinnamon chia oat pot
dishes.title: Soy yoghurt, gluten-free oats, chia seeds and cinnamon
dishes.method: Stir the oats, chia seeds and cinnamon into the soy yoghurt. Leave for five minutes to soften slightly before eating.
dishes.why: This keeps breakfast straightforward on the student's usual cooking day while soy yoghurt remains the anchor.

dishes.name: Lentil crunch cakes
dishes.title: Lentil and potato skillet, cucumber and rice cakes
dishes.method: Take the chilled skillet portion from the fridge and spoon it onto the rice cakes. Slice the cucumber and serve it alongside for contrast.
dishes.why: Yesterday's lentil preparation becomes a cool, crisp lunch rather than a repeat of the warm dinner plate.

dishes.name: Ginger tofu grain bowl
dishes.title: Warm ginger tofu, vegetables, quinoa and cucumber
dishes.method: Cook the tofu tray and quinoa during the Thursday session. Put one hot portion of each in a bowl, add sliced cucumber and finish with lemon juice. Cool and refrigerate the remaining portions promptly.
dishes.why: Hot quinoa forms a warm anchor, while cucumber keeps the midsummer dinner green and crunchy.

dishes.name: Savoury tofu crunch cakes
dishes.title: Tofu, cucumber and rice cakes with tamari
dishes.method: Pat the tofu dry and slice it thinly. Arrange it on the rice cakes with sliced cucumber and spoon over the tamari.
dishes.why: This savoury breakfast brings variety and a firm tofu anchor without adding another cooking session.

dishes.name: Lemony tofu crunch plate
dishes.title: Ginger tofu, cucumber and rice cakes
dishes.method: Eat one chilled portion of ginger tofu with sliced cucumber and rice cakes. Squeeze the lemon over the tofu just before serving.
dishes.why: The tray-baked tofu becomes a portable-feeling crunchy lunch suited to days spent building towards longer walks.

dishes.name: Hot tofu quinoa supper
dishes.title: Warm ginger tofu, vegetables and quinoa
dishes.method: Reheat the remaining tofu and quinoa portions together until piping hot, then serve immediately.
dishes.why: Reheated quinoa supplies a warm anchor and puts Friday dinner on the table with almost no work.

preparations.title: Smoky lentil and potato skillet

ingredients.term: tinned green or brown lentils, drained

preparations.method: Cut the potatoes into small cubes and slice the courgette and pepper. Heat the oil in a wide lidded pan, add the potatoes and cook for five minutes. Add the pepper, courgette, paprika and cumin and cook for another five minutes. Add the water, cover and simmer for twelve minutes, then fold in the lentils and cook uncovered for five minutes until hot and lightly saucy. Season and divide into two portions.

preparations.title: Ginger tofu and summer vegetables
preparations.method: Heat the oven to 220°C, or 200°C fan. Pat the tofu dry and cut it into cubes. Trim the beans, slice the courgette and cut the carrots into thin batons. Grate the ginger, then toss everything with the oil, tamari, paprika and pepper on a large tray. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until the tofu is browned and the vegetables retain a little bite. Divide into three portions.

preparations.title: Fluffy quinoa
preparations.method: Rinse the quinoa thoroughly. Put it in a small saucepan with the water and salt, bring to the boil, then cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat, stand covered for five minutes and fluff with a fork. Divide into two portions.

cooking_sessions.run_through: This is the extra cooking day before the student's usual Thursday session. Chop the potatoes first and start them in the wide pan; prepare the courgette and pepper while they cook, add the seasonings and water, then drain the lentils while the vegetables simmer. Finish with the lentils, eat one portion hot and refrigerate the second promptly.

Heat the oven and rinse the quinoa. Put the quinoa on the hob, then cut the tofu and vegetables and dress the tray. Roast the tray while the quinoa simmers; let the quinoa stand, turn the tray once, then portion both preparations. Eat one portion of each hot and refrigerate the Friday portions promptly.
